Teams initial strategy plan (Round 1, planning phase):

Key facts:
- seller_1 cost: 44.7, unit profit = price - 44.7
- seller_2 cost: unknown to us
- No information about seller_2's cost
- We must protect team profit, not own profit alone
- All 60 buyers always choose the lowest price among all 3 sellers
- Tied lowest prices share buyers evenly

First move: post price = 45 today (round 1)
Rationale: 45 is the minimum integer price where seller_1 breaks even. If seller_2 is also at or below 45, both are at break-even/low and buyers go to us. If seller_2 is above 45, seller_1 gets all buyers. Either way, we secure at least break-even per unit on day 1.

Round 2 planning: Team plan — we will set both our prices to 46 today. This is the minimum safe price above both our costs that maximizes per-unit profit, assuming seller_3 posts above 46 (yielding 30 buyers each for us at 156 combined). If seller_3 posts <= 46, we will recalibrate next day based on observed prices.

Team coordination for Round 3: We will both post price 46 today. This matches their previous move and is our strategy to maximize shared profit. We assume seller_3 will post above 46. If seller_3 posts at or below 46, we may need to recalibrate next day based on observed prices.

Team coordination (Round 3, planning phase):

We are in round 3. Known costs: me (seller_1) = 42.1, seller_3 = 47.9. seller_2 cost unknown.

Strategy: Stick with price 46. Rationale:
- Matches previous successful price (day 2).
- 46 - 42.1 = 3.9 profit/unit (solid margin).
- If seller_3 posts > 46, we share 30 buyers each (60 total).
- If seller_3 posts = 46, all three tie → 20 each, still strong team result.
- If seller_3 posts ≤ 46, we recalibrate next day based on observed prices.

We will NOT unilaterally lower to 45 or raise to 48, as those risks leaving us uncompetitive vs. unknown seller_2 cost without a symmetric partner.

Team plan: both post 46 today.
